name: Draftly
tagline: Turn a rough voice note into a polished product spec.
description: Draftly listens to your rambling voice memo and returns a structured spec: problem, goals, user stories and edge cases. Built for founders and PMs who think out loud but need to ship a written doc.

comments.author: Marco P.
comments.text: Used this for my whole backlog last week. Genuinely saved hours.

name: Cadence
tagline: Async standups that write themselves from your commits.
description: Cadence reads your team's git activity and drafts each person's standup automatically. Skip the meeting, keep the visibility. Integrates with GitHub, GitLab and Linear.

name: Lumina
tagline: On-brand product images from a single reference photo.
description: Upload one photo of your product and Lumina generates a full library of lifestyle, hero and social shots that keep your colours, lighting and style consistent. No prompt engineering required.

comments.author: Sara K.
comments.text: The consistency across shots is the killer feature. Others drift, this doesn't.

name: Warmly
tagline: Cold email that reads your prospect's public footprint first.
description: Warmly researches each prospect — their site, posts and recent launches — then drafts a genuinely personal opener. Higher reply rates without the copy-paste guilt.

name: Pocketbase Metrics
tagline: Privacy-first analytics you can self-host in five minutes.
description: A single binary, no cookies, GDPR-clean by default. Drop in one script tag and get the numbers that matter without shipping your visitors to an ad network.

comments.author: Raj D.
comments.text: Swapped off the big one last month. Zero regrets.

name: Snippet Vault
tagline: A searchable home for the code you keep re-writing.
description: Save, tag and instantly recall the snippets you paste into every project. Syncs across editors and lets your team share a private library.

name: Habitual
tagline: Build one habit at a time, backed by streak science.
description: Habitual refuses to let you track twenty things at once. Pick one keystone habit, get gentle nudges, and watch the streak compound. Calm by design.

comments.author: Nina B.
comments.text: The one-habit constraint is exactly why it works for me.

name: Ledgerly
tagline: Bookkeeping that closes your month while you sleep.
description: Connect your bank and Ledgerly categorises, reconciles and drafts your monthly close. Made for indie founders who'd rather build than balance.

name: Postcraft
tagline: Turn one idea into a week of on-brand posts.
description: Give Postcraft a rough thought and it spins out a week of posts tuned to your voice across X, LinkedIn and your newsletter. Schedule, tweak, done.

name: Pulse
tagline: See which marketing actually drove revenue.
description: Pulse stitches ad spend, sessions and revenue into one honest attribution view so you can kill the channels that don't pay. No 40-tab spreadsheets.

name: Nomad Desk
tagline: One membership, thousands of desks worldwide.
description: Nomad Desk gives remote workers on-demand access to vetted coworking spaces in 60+ cities on a single flexible plan. Show up, scan, sit down.

name: Chirp
tagline: An AI teammate that answers 80% of your support tickets.
description: Chirp learns from your docs and past replies, drafts answers your team approves, and quietly resolves the repetitive tickets on its own. Handover to a human is one click.

comments.author: Dana L.
comments.text: Deflection rate hit 71% for us in the first month.

name: Trackpad
tagline: Goal tracking your whole team can actually see.
description: Trackpad turns fuzzy quarterly goals into visible, updatable scorecards. Everyone knows the target, the owner and the trend at a glance.

name: Formly
tagline: Forms that feel like a conversation, not a chore.
description: Build one-question-at-a-time forms that convert, with logic, payments and a clean API. Formly is the fast, friendly way to collect anything.

name: Beacon
tagline: Uptime and error alerts that page the right human.
description: Beacon watches your endpoints and background jobs, groups the noise, and escalates only what matters to the person on call. Sleep through the false alarms.
